submissions.findingTextShort: A 2025 dose-response meta-analysis found larger blood-pressure reductions in participants with hypertension.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2025 dose-response meta-analysis of 10 randomized trials found that potassium supplementation was associated with a modest blood-pressure reduction in participants without hypertension and a larger reduction in participants with hypertension; the limited trial count and subgroup-dependent dose-response prevent a universal effect-size claim.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with and without hypertension across 10 randomized trials
submissions.usageContext: Potassium supplementation assessed through change in 24-hour urinary potassium excretion
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Only 10 RCTs met the review criteria, and effect size varied materially by hypertension status; this does not establish a single preparation-independent dose target.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2020 meta-analysis found a nonlinear potassium-blood-pressure relationship and cautioned against excessive supplementation.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A dose-response meta-analysis of 32 randomized trials found a nonlinear, approximately U-shaped relationship between potassium exposure and blood pressure, with stronger lowering effects in hypertension and higher-sodium contexts but weakening or reversal at high exposure in some analyses; this argues against interpreting more supplemental potassium as uniformly better.
submissions.populationContext: Mostly adults with hypertension in randomized trials lasting at least four weeks
submissions.usageContext: Potassium supplementation across approximately 30 to 140 mmol/day intervention ranges
submissions.uncertaintyNote: High-intake estimates were based on fewer trials and require cautious interpretation; dietary adequacy, supplementation, kidney function, and medication-related hyperkalemia risk are separate questions.

submissions.findingTextShort: In hypertension trials, potassium supplementation lowered pooled blood pressure with important sodium and treatment effect modifiers.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials in hypertensive participants found lower pooled systolic and diastolic blood pressure with potassium supplementation, with larger effects in lower-baseline-potassium, higher-sodium, higher sodium-to-potassium-ratio, and untreated subgroups; the effect should remain hypertension- and context-specific rather than generalized to all users.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with hypertension in randomized supplementation trials of at least four weeks
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Effect modification by baseline intake, sodium exposure, region, and antihypertensive treatment limits a single universal magnitude estimate.

submissions.findingTextShort: A randomized double-blind trial found fatigue and cognition signals from 2 g/day levocarnitine in centenarians.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: In a placebo-controlled randomized double-blind trial of 66 centenarians with fatigue, 2 g/day oral levocarnitine was associated with improvements in physical fatigue, mental fatigue, fatigue-severity scores, selected body-composition measures, and MMSE compared with placebo; the extreme-age population prevents generalization to routine fatigue in younger or otherwise healthy adults.
submissions.populationContext: Sixty-six centenarians with fatigue after slight physical activity
submissions.usageContext: Oral levocarnitine 2 g once daily versus placebo
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small, highly selected extreme-age population; this is L-carnitine/levocarnitine evidence and must not be merged into acetyl-L-carnitine or propionyl-L-carnitine evidence ownership.

submissions.findingTextShort: Lower-risk pooled evidence did not show a significant benefit of carnitine for cancer-related fatigue.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review and meta-analysis of carnitine supplementation for cancer-related fatigue found that lower-risk pooled studies did not show a significant fatigue reduction versus control, despite positive findings in several weaker or nonrandomized studies; this condition-specific null result is an important counterweight to broad fatigue claims.
submissions.populationContext: People with cancer-related fatigue across heterogeneous clinical studies
submissions.usageContext: Carnitine supplementation in oncology-related fatigue contexts
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This finding is condition-specific and does not negate the centenarian trial, but it prevents a preparation- and population-independent fatigue-efficacy claim.

submissions.findingTextShort: L-carnitine fatigue evidence remains too population- and indication-specific for a generic fatigue grade.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The available fatigue literature spans highly selected centenarians, oncology populations, variable study quality, and heterogeneous carnitine interventions; broader fatigue claims require better replicated trials that preserve L-carnitine formulation identity and population context rather than borrowing from acetyl-L-carnitine or other carnitine forms.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This is a scope and replication gap, not evidence that L-carnitine has no effect in every population.

submissions.findingTextShort: PMID 34376917 tested anthocyanin plus astaxanthin plus lutein, so it cannot isolate astaxanthin efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 34376917 is a randomized placebo-controlled study of a multi-ingredient test food containing anthocyanin, astaxanthin, and lutein in adults with visual-display-related eye fatigue; any eye-function signal from this study must remain combination-specific and cannot be attributed to astaxanthin alone.
submissions.populationContext: Healthy Japanese adults with eye fatigue after visual display terminal use
submissions.usageContext: Combination product containing anthocyanin, astaxanthin, and lutein for six weeks
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The intervention is intrinsically multi-ingredient and sponsor-linked, so isolated astaxanthin attribution is not supported by this trial design.

submissions.findingTextShort: A skin-aging meta-analysis found moisture and elasticity signals but no significant wrinkle-depth reduction.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review and meta-analysis of human astaxanthin studies found significant pooled improvements in skin moisture and elasticity with oral supplementation, while wrinkle depth was not significantly reduced versus placebo; heterogeneity, small studies, and mixed oral/topical evidence limit broad anti-aging claims.
submissions.populationContext: Adults in randomized oral trials plus smaller open-label topical or oral-topical studies
submissions.usageContext: Astaxanthin used orally and, in some nonrandomized studies, topically or in combined routes
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Outcome-specific results differ: moisture and elasticity signals should not be rewritten as a general wrinkle-reduction or global anti-aging effect.

submissions.findingTextShort: Astaxanthin improved selected oxidative/inflammatory biomarkers, while CRP and TNF-alpha were not significantly changed.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A meta-analysis of 12 randomized placebo-controlled trials found lower malondialdehyde overall and an interleukin-6 signal in type 2 diabetes, but effects on C-reactive protein and tumor necrosis factor-alpha were not significant and data for several other biomarkers were limited; this supports selected biomarker effects rather than a broad anti-inflammatory clinical-benefit claim.
submissions.populationContext: Three hundred eighty participants across heterogeneous randomized trials, including type 2 diabetes and overweight subgroups
submissions.usageContext: Astaxanthin supplementation for at least one week versus placebo
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Biomarker changes are not equivalent to patient-important clinical outcomes, and several signals were subgroup-specific or based on few trials.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 meta-analysis found CK/LDH recovery-marker signals but no significant improvement in major exercise-performance outcomes.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 randomized trials found lower creatine kinase and lactate dehydrogenase recovery markers with astaxanthin, while VO2max, time-trial performance, and maximal workload or power were not significantly improved; the LDH result had substantial heterogeneity and should not be converted into a performance-enhancement claim.
submissions.populationContext: Participants in randomized exercise, recovery, and performance trials
submissions.usageContext: Oral astaxanthin supplementation versus placebo or control across varied doses, durations, and exercise protocols
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Recovery biomarkers and direct performance outcomes diverged; dosing, protocol, and outcome heterogeneity remain substantial.

submissions.findingTextShort: Astaxanthin trials need better standardization of dose, duration, formulation, exercise protocol, and patient-important outcomes.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Across recent astaxanthin meta-analyses, heterogeneity in dose, duration, population, formulation, exercise protocol, and outcome selection limits stable clinical grading; future trials should distinguish biomarker recovery from direct performance or patient-important outcomes and preserve standalone versus combination-product identity.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This is a research-design gap and should not be represented as evidence of either benefit or harm.
